steps.note: a 132x50 terminal prints the 1378-byte stream, then the title oracle-vt-fed
the title comes after the stream, so the parser has taken every byte of it

argv: d() { if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$1" | sha256sum; else printf '%s' "$1" | shasum -a 256; fi; }; printf '\033]2;vt:%.64s screen:%.64s\007' "$(d "$1")" "$(d "$2")"

steps.note: a second terminal titles itself vt:<sha256 of the VT state> screen:<sha256 of the screen text>; it starts in / because a new terminal otherwise inherits the folder the stream's OSC 7 reported, which does not exist
the settled checkpoint holds the hash terminal's title: the arms and the baseline compare it

invariants: generated by schemas/terminal-corpus/generate.py (p15-oracle-101); features: wide, graphemes, variation-selectors, mode-2027, ich-dch, no-autowrap
the VT state and screen of the stream terminal hash to the same title on both terminal-holder arms
teardown: verify the socket and state root are gone
